'''Spencer Charles Hilton Barrett''' {{post-nominals|country=UK|FRS}} {{post-nominals|FRSC}} (born June 7, 1948)<ref name=whoswho/> is a Canadian evolutionary biologist, formerly a [[Canada Research Chair]] at [[University of Toronto]] and, in 2010, was named Extraordinary Professor at [[University of Stellenbosch]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=613 |title=Spencer Barrett |publisher=gc.ca |access-date=December 18, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://labs.eeb.utoronto.ca/BarrettLab/Sbarrett.html |title=Spencer Barrett |publisher=utoronto.ca |access-date=December 18, 2016}}</ref> He is currently University Professor Emeritus at the University of Toronto.

==Education==
Barrett attended [[University of Reading]] in [[England]] for his undergraduate education.<ref name=whoswho/> He then received his graduate degree at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he was supervised by [[Herbert George Baker|Herbert G. Baker]] and defended his [[PhD]] thesis in 1977, focused on the plant breeding systems in ''[[Eichhornia]]'' and ''[[Pontederia]] species.''<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Spencer Charles Hilton|last=Barrett |title=Breeding systems in Eichhornia and Pontederia, tristylous genera of the Pontederiaceae |publisher=University of California, Berkeley |date=1977 |oclc=6180836 |id={{ProQuest|302835946}}}}</ref><ref name=orcid>Spencer Barrett's {{ORCID|0000-0002-7762-3455}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Barrett's interests are in [[evolutionary biology]], [[Extended evolutionary synthesis|evolutionary genetics]], [[evolutionary ecology]] and [[plant reproduction]].<ref name=googlescholar/> His research seeks understanding of how flowers evolve and what mechanisms are responsible for [[mating system]] transitions in [[flowering plant]]s.<ref name= frs/> Since 2017, he has served as [[Editor-in-Chief]] of the ''[[Proceedings of the Royal Society]]'' series B,<ref name=Barrett2017>{{cite journal|last1=Barrett|first1=Spencer C. H.|title=Proceedings B 2016: the year in review|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences|volume=284|issue=1846|year=2017|article-number=20162633|issn=0962-8452|doi=10.1098/rspb.2016.2633|pmid=28053056|pmc=5247507}}</ref> the flagship [[scientific journal]] in the biological sciences of the [[Royal Society]].

Barrett is an evolutionary biologist and a worldwide authority on the ecology and genetics of plant reproduction. His work has focused on increasing understanding of how flowers evolve and the mechanisms responsible for mating system transitions in flowering plants.

Barrett provided the first experimental evidence for the purging of deleterious genes following inbreeding in plants.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Barrett |first=S. C. H. |last2=Charlesworth |first2=D. |date=August 1991 |title=Effects of a change in the level of inbreeding on the genetic load |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/352522a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=352 |issue=6335 |pages=522–524 |doi=10.1038/352522a0 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also demonstrated that self-fertilization owing to large floral displays in plants can have a detrimental effect on the male fertility of plants.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Harder |first=Lawrence D. |last2=Barrett |first2=Spencer C. H. |date=February 1995 |title=Mating cost of large floral displays in hermaphrodite plants |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/373512a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=373 |issue=6514 |pages=512–515 |doi=10.1038/373512a0 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Barrett's research group at the University of Toronto focuses on understanding the mechanisms responsible for the evolution of plant mating strategies, and he has edited several leading books in the field.

==Awards and honours==
Barrett was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] in 1998 and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of London]] in 2004.<ref name=frs/> He is a founding member of the Canadian Society for Ecology and Evolution and its President from 2010 to 2011.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/spencer-barrett-11038/|title=Professor Spencer Barrett|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=The Royal Society:Fellows Directory|year=2014|location=London}}</ref>

In 2006 the Canadian Botanical Association awarded him the George Lawson Medal for lifetime achievement in botany.<ref>{{cite web|title=Past Recipients of the Lawson Medal|website=Canadian Botanical Association/L'Association Botanique du Canada|url=https://www.cba-abc.ca/awards/the-lawson-medal/past-recipients-of-the-lawson-medal}}</ref> In 2008 he received the [[Sewall Wright Award]] from the [[American Society of Naturalists]].<ref name=frs/> In 2014, he received the [[Flavelle Medal]] from the Royal Society of Canada.<ref>[https://rsc-src.ca/en/past-award-winners#Flavelle Past Award Winners: The Flavelle Medal]</ref> In 2020 the [[Linnean Society of London]] award him the [[Darwin–Wallace Medal]].<ref name=frs/>

In 2009 he was elected as a Foreign Honorary Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-06 |title=Spencer Charles Hilton Barrett {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/spencer-charles-hilton-barrett |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref> In April 2020 Spencer Barrett was elected an International Member (Foreign Associate) of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020|title=2020 NAS Election|website=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref>
